name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed rise fully priced; yen ~158.5/$
summary: Markets fully price a December Fed rate rise as Waller floats 50bp; Japan warns on the yen but has not intervened
state: Minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed almost all officials saw further tightening as likely appropriate, and fed funds futures on 18 Nov fully priced a 25bp rise in December, with Governor Waller saying a 50bp move should be considered (FXStreet/UOB). Japan's finance minister Katayama said around 13 Nov that Tokyo will coordinate with the US Treasury on one-sided yen moves near 160 (investingLive); the yen was about 158.5 per dollar on 22 Nov. No intervention or emergency move was found, so this remains a stagflationary dilemma at Watch.
for_you: Higher policy rates in the US, UK and euro area keep borrowing costs for mortgages and business loans elevated. Japanese warnings mean sharp yen swings are possible around official statements.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma (Fed raising into slowdown) = Watch; no inter-meeting move or intervention (Alert)

sources.title: FXStreet — Federal Reserve: hawkish path priced in (UOB)
investingLive — Japan's Katayama warns of one-sided yen moves near 160, will coordinate with US Treasury

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
